# buddy-agent-harness

> Initialize standards-based agent configuration across agent harnesses. The npm package `buddy-agent-harness` ships a CLI, an agent plugin's skills, and a library.

Generated by `packages/buddy-agent-harness/scripts/generate-llms-txt.ts` (`pnpm --filter buddy-agent-harness llms:gen`) from the command tree, the shipped skills, the library entry, and the docs site. Edit the generator or its sources, not this file.

A repository keeps one canonical agent configuration — a root `AGENTS.md` and an `.agents/` tree, with skills in `.agents/skills/` — and harnesses that cannot read it directly get bridges to it.

Of the CLI's top-level commands, `doctor` and `governance` say they are read-only; `init`, `mcp`, `dep-plugins`, and `reference` can write.

Every runnable command takes `--format` with `toon`, `json`, or `text`; the default is `toon`, except that `reference show`, `reference create`, `reference delete`, and `governance show` default to `text`.

Documentation site: [One canonical agent configuration](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/).

## CLI

- [CLI Overview](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/cli/): The buddy-agent-harness command line, and when to use it instead of the skill.
- [`buddy-agent-harness init`](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/cli/init/): Set up canonical agent skills for the harnesses already enabled in a repository.
- [`buddy-agent-harness doctor`](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/cli/doctor/): Report whether this repository's harness bridges still resolve — skills into .agents/skills, instructions into AGENTS.md — and whether each harness's user-scope file loads ~/.agents/AGENTS.md. Read-only.
- [`buddy-agent-harness mcp`](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/cli/mcp/): Work with the golden MCP server set at .agents/buddy-agent-harness/mcp.toml.
- [`buddy-agent-harness mcp project`](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/cli/mcp/): Project the golden MCP server set into each enabled harness. A dry run unless --write; never overwrites a change made on the harness side.
- [`buddy-agent-harness mcp reconcile`](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/cli/mcp/): Import a harness-side MCP change into the golden set, one approved field at a time. A dry run unless --accept names a field.
- [`buddy-agent-harness dep-plugins`](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/cli/dep-plugins/): Derive the marketplace catalog for plugins shipped by this repository’s dependencies, so a harness can install them. Writes the catalog; installing is the harness’s own job.
- [`buddy-agent-harness reference`](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/cli/reference/): Read on-demand reference documents by name, layered across the managed, project, user, and plugin tiers, and start or delete one in the project or user tier.
- [`buddy-agent-harness reference show`](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/cli/reference/): Print one or more references, each resolved through the tiers and combined as its layers ask.
- [`buddy-agent-harness reference list`](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/cli/reference/): List every layer, and every reference at every layer that holds it, marked used or shadowed.
- [`buddy-agent-harness reference search`](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/cli/reference/): Find references by name, description, tags, headings, or body, best match first.
- [`buddy-agent-harness reference where`](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/cli/reference/): List the project and user files an override of a reference can be written to, highest precedence first, with the copy each overrides and who it applies to.
- [`buddy-agent-harness reference create`](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/cli/reference/): Start a new reference in the project or user tier from a template, marked merge-sections when it overrides a copy below. Never overwrites.
- [`buddy-agent-harness reference delete`](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/cli/reference/): Delete the project or user copy of a reference, and report which copy answers the name afterwards. Never deletes a plugin-shipped or managed copy.
- [`buddy-agent-harness governance`](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/cli/governance/): Deprecated: use `reference`. Read the governance documents the project, user, and machine-wide override layers hold. Read-only.
- [`buddy-agent-harness governance list`](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/cli/governance/): List every governance the override layers hold, each at the layer that would win.
- [`buddy-agent-harness governance show`](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/cli/governance/): Print one governance document, resolved through the layers in order.

## Skills

- [Skills](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/skills/): The skills the plugin ships, init, doctor, enhance and repair, the reference skill it brings with it, and when to run the CLI instead.
- [`doctor-buddy-agent-harness`](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/skills/doctor-buddy-agent-harness/): Use this skill when a repository loads no project skills, when skills are missing after a clone, when a harness appears to be ignoring AGENTS.md, or when checking whether the agent configuration bridges into .claude/skills and the other harness files still resolve.
- [`enhance`](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/skills/enhance/): Use this skill when a repository already has an AGENTS.md and you want to add guidance it is missing, or to refresh a vetted section it carries in an outdated form — offering each one at a time and writing only what the user approves. Runs on its own or straight after init.
- [`init-buddy-agent-harness`](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/skills/init-buddy-agent-harness/): Use this skill when initializing, adopting, or migrating a repository's agent configuration to the open AGENTS.md and Agent Skills standards, so one canonical source works across Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot CLI, and other agent harnesses.
- [`repair`](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/skills/repair/): Use this skill when a repository's agent configuration is present but wrong or outdated — a retired harness name, a git-ignored bridge, an AGENTS.local.md nothing reads, a skill a harness refuses to load, or an MCP server that differs between the golden set and a harness, on the side that is plainly ahead. Runs doctor to find them, then offers each correction with its before and after and writes only what is approved.

## Getting started

- [Introduction](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/getting-started/introduction/): Keep one repository-owned agent configuration that every agent harness can read.
- [Migrating Existing Configuration](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/getting-started/migrating/): Consolidate CLAUDE.md, .cursor/rules, and per-harness skill directories into one canonical source.

## Agent configuration

- [Agent Configuration Best Practices](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/agent-configuration/best-practices/): Practices that apply across AGENTS.md, skills, and harness bridges, starting with the cost of every file an agent has to go and open.
- [Harness Differences](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/agent-configuration/harness-differences/): Which agent harnesses read canonical configuration directly, and which need a bridge.
- [Claude Code](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/agent-configuration/harnesses/claude-code/): Claude Code needs a skills projection, and reads AGENTS.md itself unless a CLAUDE.md beside it suppresses it.
- [Cursor](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/agent-configuration/harnesses/cursor/): Cursor reads .agents/skills and AGENTS.md natively, in every mode.
- [Gemini CLI](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/agent-configuration/harnesses/gemini-cli/): Gemini CLI reads .agents/skills at both scopes, and needs AGENTS.md added to context.fileName.
- [What Belongs in AGENTS.md](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/agent-configuration/instruction-files/): Why an instruction file is a recurring context cost, which lines earn that cost, and where everything else should live.
- [Instruction Purpose](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/agent-configuration/instruction-purpose/): What a block of instruction is for (procedure, criteria, policy, reference, menu, tone, or structure), and why separating them makes instructions composable.
- [Instruction Target](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/agent-configuration/instruction-target/): Which of the agent's outputs an instruction governs (a produced artifact, this session's conversation, or another agent's context), and why separating them lets contradictory instructions coexist.
- [Lookup Files](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/agent-configuration/lookup-files/): A convention for giving a portable skill the project-specific pointers it needs: where to look for content of a given kind, without paying for it every session.
- [MCP Servers](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/agent-configuration/mcp-servers/): The user-authored golden set of MCP servers: where it lives, how doctor compares it against each harness copy, and the credential policy.
- [Open Standards](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/agent-configuration/open-standards/): AGENTS.md, Agent Skills, and how much authority the .agents/skills convention actually has.
- [Writing Portable Skills](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/agent-configuration/portable-skills/): Which SKILL.md frontmatter survives across harnesses, and which two mistakes silently drop a skill.
- [References and Skills](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/agent-configuration/references/): When supplementary instructions belong in a reference fetched by name rather than in a skill, and how layered references combine.
- [Skill Scripts](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/agent-configuration/skill-scripts/): How a skill runs a script that ships beside it, and why the download fallback stays.
- [Commands](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/agent-configuration/skills/commands/): User-invoked slash-command workflows, the two mechanisms that create one, and why neither is portable.
- [Direct Invocation Skill](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/agent-configuration/skills/direct-skill/): A skill selected by another skill naming it outright, never by matching a user's situation. The minimal-description rule that enforces it portably, and why it is not "internal."
- [Gateway Skill](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/agent-configuration/skills/gateway-skill/): Workflow entrypoints that activate an opt-in workflow, gather missing intent, and route, and why the routing effect is what distinguishes them.
- [Kinds of Skill](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/agent-configuration/skills/overview/): Commands, gateways, personas, and by-name skills are all SKILL.md files. The three axes that actually distinguish them, and which distinctions survive between harnesses.
- [Persona](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/agent-configuration/skills/persona/): Agent identity definitions that bundle role, expertise, permissions, and constraints, and why they are canonical-only configuration rather than something this project projects.
- [Responsibility](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/agent-configuration/skills/responsibility/): The Required / Optional / Delegated axis, covering what an agent-configuration artifact must do itself, may optionally add, or hands to a named role via dependency inversion.

## Reference

- [Configuration Layout](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/reference/configuration-layout/): What initialization puts on disk, and why it records nothing else.
- [Glossary](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/reference/glossary/): The terms this documentation uses for canonical configuration, harnesses, projections, and kinds of skill.
- [Sources & Confidence](https://repobuddy.github.io/buddy-agent-harness/sources/): How well-sourced each harness claim is, and which ones are not established.
